principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.3.1 Info & Relationships; WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices — Grid Pattern
location: /library — LibraryTable (src/components/library/LibraryTable.tsx): outer scroller has role="grid", inner header row + data rows have role="row", but no cell uses role="columnheader" or role="gridcell"
problem: The 7,144-row paint grid declares role="grid" + role="row" but ZERO descendants carry role="columnheader", role="rowheader", or role="gridcell". Screen readers cannot navigate by column or announce headers ("Brand: AK Interactive, Name: 3b Au Basic Protector"). The grid is announced as a flat list of cell text only. This is the highest-traffic surface in the app and the most data-dense — it is opaque to AT users.
fix: In TableHeader: change each <span> to role="columnheader". In PaintRow: change each <span> cell to role="gridcell". Set aria-colcount on the grid container and aria-colindex on each cell so column navigation announces correctly. Keep the existing aria-label values ("Type", "Owned", "Wishlisted") on the columnheaders. No layout change required — pure role swap.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of System Status; Refactoring UI — Color is not the only channel; Universal — never use color/state alone as the sole differentiator
location: /wishlist — status filter pills (Wanted / Bought / Cancelled / All) and category pills (Any / Box / Bits / Paint / Tool / Terrain / Other); /tools/match — brand-filter chips (AK INTERACTIVE / CITADEL / etc.)
problem: Active and inactive filter pills render with identical visual treatment — same color rgb(245,247,248), same font-weight 400, no background, no border, no underline. The only difference is aria-pressed="true" vs "false". Sighted users cannot tell which filter is currently applied; the only cue is the result count silently updating in the table below. Verified on Wishlist (Wanted is the default-active filter but reads identical to Bought) and on Tools/Match (clicking CITADEL filters to 382 results but the CITADEL chip itself shows no visible state change).
fix: Give aria-pressed="true" / data-active="true" pills a visible distinction matching the rest of the app's chip pattern: cyan-text + cyan-border + 8-10% cyan background tint (the same recipe FilterRail uses successfully). Single Tailwind variant addition; one shared chipClass utility covers both Wishlist filters and Match brand chips. Optional: bold or underline the active label for redundancy with users who customise contrast.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency & Standards; Jakob's Law (users expect modal dialogs to be centered with a dimmed backdrop)
location: /recipes/[id] — Share Recipe modal (<dialog> element opened via showModal()); same brokenness affects /recipes/[id] Delete confirm; observed at native <dialog> render inside the .max-w-7xl space-y-6 page wrapper
problem: The Share Recipe modal opens stuck to the top-left of the viewport with no visible backdrop dim, occupying ~half the screen as a left-edge panel. Expected: a centered card with a black/60 backdrop. Native <dialog>.showModal() should auto-center, but Tailwind classes on the <dialog> include no centering utilities (only max-w-2xl w-[95vw]) and the backdrop styling (backdrop:bg-black/70) is not visibly applied. As a result, the modal looks like a dropped panel rather than a focused dialog, and the rest of the page is still tappable/distracting behind it.
fix: On the <dialog> element add Tailwind classes `m-auto inset-0 max-h-[90vh]` (so browser dialog centering kicks in), keep `max-w-2xl w-[95vw]`, and verify `backdrop:bg-black/70` survives Tailwind 4 pseudo-element prefix compilation (Tailwind 4 changed `backdrop:` syntax — may need `[&::backdrop]:bg-black/70` or a global stylesheet rule for `dialog::backdrop`). Confirm in DevTools that `dialog::backdrop` paints when `showModal()` is called.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 Reflow; CSS containing-block specification (transform/filter/backdrop-filter creates a new containing block for fixed-positioned descendants)
location: Global — sticky footer used on all tool pages (<footer class="sticky bottom-0 z-10 ... backdrop-blur ..." aria-label="Tool actions">) and the shared SendToRecipeModal (role="dialog" class="fixed inset-0 z-30 flex items-center justify-center p-4 bg-black/60")
problem: On /tools/wheel, /tools/match, /tools/eyedropper, /tools/gradient the shared 'Send to recipe' modal opens trapped inside the sticky footer's box — a 1080×56px strip at the bottom of the viewport — instead of covering the full screen. Cause: the sticky <footer> has `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)`, which per CSS spec creates a containing block for ALL fixed-position descendants. The modal's `fixed inset-0` no longer means 'fill the viewport'; it means 'fill the footer's box.' The backdrop dim also clips to the footer, defeating modal focus.
fix: Either (a) portal the modal outside the footer subtree to <body> using React's createPortal so it renders as a sibling of <main>, or (b) drop `backdrop-blur` from the sticky footer (use `bg-[var(--color-bg)]/95` solid only). Option (a) is the correct architectural fix because the modal is logically global; option (b) is a one-class workaround. Either resolves the containing-block trap.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A — all functionality available from keyboard); Drag and Drop accessibility guidance
location: /recipes/[id] — ZoneList (zone rows use HTML5 <li draggable="true"> with `cursor-grab` ≡ handle, title="Drag to reorder"); StepList likely identical pattern; sighted-only "DRAG = TO REORDER" caption above the step list
problem: Zone and step reordering is implemented via HTML5 native drag-and-drop. There is no keyboard equivalent — no arrow-key move, no 'Move up / Move down' button, no aria-grabbed/dropeffect pattern. The visible affordance reads 'DRAG = TO REORDER' which doubly excludes keyboard-only users. A painter using a touch device without precise dragging (assistive switch user, reduced-mobility user) also cannot reorder a recipe.
fix: Add a keyboard-accessible reorder mechanism on each row. Cheapest pattern: two icon buttons per row — '▲ Move up' / '▼ Move down' (or 'Move zone Armor up') — visible on focus/hover, aria-labeled, that call the same reorder action as the drag. Update the caption to 'DRAG OR USE THE ▲▼ BUTTONS TO REORDER'. The drag handle ≡ should also become a real button with role="button" + aria-label so screen readers announce the row as reorderable.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.3.1 Info & Relationships; HTML living standard — heading order should not skip levels
location: /library — FilterRail Section component renders every section title as <h3> directly under the page <h1>; /tools/match — the results grid uses no semantic table; /recipes/[id] — the recipe TITLE ('Untitled recipe', 28px green) is a <div>, not an <h1>
problem:
Heading hierarchy is broken on multiple core routes. (a) /library has

LIBRARY

followed directly by

SEARCH

,

HEX

,

TYPE

, etc. — h2 is skipped. (b) /recipes/[id] has NO

at all — the visually-largest text 'Untitled recipe' is a plain
; the document outline starts at h3 ('ZONES · 0', 'NOTES'). Screen reader users navigating by headings get a broken outline that doesn't match the visual hierarchy. The h2s that do exist on /recipes/[id] are dialog titles ('Share recipe', 'Delete recipe?') which are out of document flow.
fix: (a) In FilterRail.Section change `<h3>` to `<h2>` (page sections under the h1). (b) In RecipeHeader change the recipe-name <div> to `<h1>` with the same styling (a div-as-heading is purely a tag swap). Confirm the heading outline becomes: Recipe name (h1) → Zones, Steps, Notes (h2). Apply the same Section→h2 pattern wherever a page has a single h1 + multiple grouped sections.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.3.1 Info & Relationships; WCAG 2.2 §4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
location: /tools/match — entire results pane ("<div class='grid grid-cols-[24px_1fr_72px_56px]'>" header + per-row siblings, NO role assigned); /tools/gradient — SHADOW/BASE/HIGHLIGHT hex inputs (placeholder-only labelling, no <label>, no aria-label)
problem: Two separate semantic gaps on the tool routes: (1) /tools/match renders its results table as plain <div> grid with sibling rows — no role="table"/"row"/"columnheader"/"cell". A screen reader hears 'AK Interactive Deep Blue PAINT delta-E 1.8 USE' as one run-on text node, with no column context. Inspection: querySelectorAll('[role="columnheader"]') = 0; querySelectorAll('[role="row"]') = 0. (2) /tools/gradient hex inputs (#072547, #0E4A8A, #4A9EFF) have no <label>, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby — only a placeholder duplicating the value. Screen readers announce three identical 'edit text' fields. The visible SHADOW / BASE / HIGHLIGHT captions are sibling <h3> headings, not associated.
fix: (1) /tools/match: wrap the results in <table>/<thead>/<tbody>/<tr>/<th scope="col">/<td> (or add the role= attributes to the existing divs). (2) /tools/gradient: wrap each hex input in <label> with the visible 'SHADOW' / 'BASE' / 'HIGHLIGHT' text, or add aria-label="Shadow hex"/"Base hex"/"Highlight hex" on each input. Both fixes are mechanical.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency & Standards; Apple HIG / Material 3 — top-level app navigation should not leak into public/marketing surfaces
location: /r/[slug] — public recipe view; cause is global layout (src/app/layout.tsx) unconditionally rendering <NavRail /> regardless of route or session
problem: An unauthenticated visitor landing on a shared recipe URL sees the full authenticated sidebar: Projects, Library, Recipes, Tools, Wishlist, User. Every one of those links bounces them to /sign-in, turning a sharing surface into a frustration funnel. The page also adds a separate public header (left-padded 'Mini Manager' + SIGN IN top-right), so the visitor now has TWO sets of navigation chrome competing for attention. Both PublicRecipeView CTAs ('[ EDIT IN MINI MANAGER ]' going to /recipes/<id> and '[ OPEN MINI MANAGER ]' going to /) are also bounce-to-sign-in for the same logged-out reader.
fix: In src/app/layout.tsx, conditionally render <NavRail /> + <BottomTabBar /> only when a session exists, OR move them out of the root layout into an authenticated route-group layout (src/app/(app)/layout.tsx) and put public routes (/r/*, /sign-in) into src/app/(public)/layout.tsx with their own slim header. Rename the CTAs to action-truthful labels: '[ CLONE TO MY LIBRARY ]' (instead of EDIT IN MINI MANAGER) and drop '[ OPEN MINI MANAGER ]' in favour of a single sign-up upsell card explaining what Mini Manager does.

principle: WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices — Tabs pattern; NN/g #4 Consistency & Standards
location: /recipes/[id] paint-slot popover — LIBRARY / CUSTOM HEX tabs render as <button aria-pressed="true|false">; shared SendToRecipeModal — EXISTING RECIPE / NEW RECIPE tabs render the same way
problem: Two parallel tab UIs (paint picker, send-to-recipe modal) are implemented as a row of toggle buttons with aria-pressed instead of the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern (role="tablist" / role="tab" / role="tabpanel" / aria-selected / arrow-key navigation). Screen readers announce them as 'pressed/unpressed toggle button' rather than 'tab N of 2, selected', and arrow keys do not switch tabs. This is functional but doesn't match the pattern users expect from every other tabbed UI on the web (Jakob's Law).
fix: Introduce a small <Tabs> primitive with role="tablist" wrapping role="tab" buttons (each with aria-selected + aria-controls + roving tabindex), and role="tabpanel" wrappers around the swap-in content. Reuse on both surfaces. Arrow-key navigation between tabs is ~8 LOC.

principle: NN/g #9 Help users recognize/diagnose/recover from errors; Polaris / Refactoring UI — empty states must distinguish 'no data yet' from 'no data matches'
location: /wishlist — empty-state row 'No wishlist items match the current filters.' shown when there are zero items at all (not when filters are applied)
problem: On a fresh /wishlist with zero items and default filters, the empty state reads 'No wishlist items match the current filters.' This wrongly implies the user has applied filters that need clearing. A first-time visitor reads it as 'something is hiding my items' rather than 'I haven't added anything yet'. There is no first-use guidance (no 'Paste a vendor URL above to add your first item' message, no CTA, no example) — unlike /recipes which has a strong first-use empty state.
fix: Branch the empty state on hasActiveFilters: when filters ARE active, keep 'No wishlist items match the current filters. [ Clear filters ]'. When the wishlist is genuinely empty, show: 'Nothing on your shopping list yet. Paste a vendor URL above, or type a title to add manually.' Mirror the /recipes empty-state structure for consistency.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.4.7 Focus Visible; WCAG 2.2 §1.3.1 Info & Relationships
location: /library — column-header cell labelled only 'T'; /wishlist — column-header labelled only 'P' (Priority, but never spelled out)
problem: Both table surfaces collapse a column to a single letter to save horizontal space: 'T' for Type on /library, 'P' for Priority on /wishlist. /library handles this correctly — the header span carries aria-label="Type" and each row cell carries aria-label="Paint"/etc. /wishlist's 'P' column header has no aria-label and no title; sighted users cannot recover the meaning unless they open a row's detail drawer and notice the PRIORITY field. The visual confusion is exacerbated because 'P' could equally be Project, Price, or Paint to a returning user.
fix: On /wishlist add aria-label="Priority" + title="Priority" to the P column header, and either (a) widen the column enough to show 'PRI' or 'PRIORITY' on desktop and only collapse to 'P' below the md breakpoint, or (b) replace the letter with a small priority icon (▴▾ or ●) with title/aria-label intact. Consistency with /library's aria-labeled single-letter column is the minimum bar.

principle: Refactoring UI — Consistency of visual system; Vintage Terminal/CRT §9 — every interactive element should adopt the aesthetic, no default-OS chrome leaking through
location: /tools/wheel L* slider (input[type=range], default WebKit/Firefox blue thumb + track); /tools/gradient STEPS slider (same); /wishlist price input (default browser number spinner)
problem: Native HTML range sliders and number-spinner controls render with the OS default appearance — bright blue track, round grey thumb, OS-native spinner arrows. Against the green/cyan phosphor palette these read as foreign elements and break the carefully-built CRT aesthetic. The L* slider is particularly prominent (sits directly under the colour wheel and is the only meaningful saturation/value input).
fix: Restyle native sliders with the existing palette: `accent-color: var(--color-green)` covers the simple case; for full custom appearance use the project's existing chip pattern (1px green track, 12px square cyan thumb, focus ring). Hide native number-spinner arrows on the price input with `appearance-none` and provide explicit + / − buttons (consistent with the OWNED − 0 + pattern already used elsewhere in the app). One shared utility class for all sliders.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) — interactive controls must be at least 24×24 CSS pixels
location: /library — owned (✗) and wishlist (☆) toggle buttons in each row (measured 36×17px and 28×17px); /library — collapsed brand A-Z group buttons (215×17px); /r/[slug] — '[ OPEN MINI MANAGER ]' link (177×17px)
problem: Several interactive controls measure 17px tall — below WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8's 24×24 floor. The library Own/Wishlist toggles are the worst offender because (a) they appear in every one of 7,144 rows, (b) they are the primary inventory affordance on the most-used surface, and (c) a 17px target on a mobile screen is at the edge of dismiss-by-accident range. The brand A-Z accordion summaries and the public-page '[ OPEN MINI MANAGER ]' link are 17px tall for the same reason — text without vertical padding.
fix: Add `min-h-[24px]` (or the existing `tap-target` utility class, which Ross already uses elsewhere) to: InventoryControls compact-variant buttons, CollapsibleBrandList summary buttons, and PublicRecipeView '[ OPEN MINI MANAGER ]' link. Vertical padding of py-1 typically brings 17px text to 25px without breaking row density. Confirm row heights still feel dense on /library (the 40px ROW_HEIGHT constant gives plenty of room).

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A); §4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
location: /tools/wheel — colour wheel <canvas role="img" aria-label="Colour wheel"> is the primary hue/saturation picker; only alternative entry is the L* lightness slider — no hex/numeric input for hue or saturation
problem: The colour wheel canvas is the only way to pick hue and saturation, and it accepts only mouse/touch drag. There is no keyboard alternative: no hex text input, no H/S numeric fields, no arrow-key control of the picker dot. Keyboard-only and screen-reader users can change the lightness via the L* slider but cannot pick a colour. WCAG 2.1.1 requires all functionality to be operable by keyboard.
fix: Add a hex input below the wheel (mirror the /tools/match pattern — small swatch + hex text input that commits on Enter/blur). Optional secondary: arrow-key control of the wheel-picker dot when the canvas has focus (left/right = hue, up/down = saturation). The hex input alone discharges the WCAG obligation and is the cheaper fix.

principle: Polaris / Refactoring UI — design for real content; NN/g #2 Match between system and real world
location: /r/[slug] — public recipe view OG meta + page heading; affects every shared link of an unnamed recipe
problem:
Recipes default to the name 'Untitled recipe' and the share flow does not require naming. A recipe published without a name produces an OG title 'Untitled recipe', a page

Untitled recipe

, and an OG image with that text. Every shared link from a hurried user looks like a placeholder, making the social-share/Reddit-post flow feel low-effort. Combined with the equally undescriptive OG description ('A paint recipe shared via Mini Manager — 1 zone, infantry.'), the previews carry zero information that would make a viewer click.
fix: Either (a) force a name field at publish time — disable [ PUBLISH ] until the recipe has a non-default name, with inline 'Name your recipe before sharing' hint, or (b) synthesise a descriptive fallback when name === 'Untitled recipe': 'Infantry recipe · 1 zone · 1 step' for OG title, and the first step's paint description for OG description. (a) is preventative (Heuristic #5 Error Prevention), (b) is graceful degradation. (a) preferred.

principle: Refactoring UI — Hierarchy through size + spacing; Apple HIG Clarity
location: /r/[slug] — between the INFANTRY · 1 zone meta row and the ARMOR zone card, a tiny orphan 16px blue swatch (the recipe's first paint hex) sits with no caption, no label, no context
problem: On a public recipe view a 16×16px blue square floats between the title meta-row and the first zone card, with whitespace above and below. There is no caption or aria-label, no obvious relationship to the rest of the content. It reads as a layout glitch or a broken image. (It is actually the recipe's representative/first-step swatch, but that intent is not communicated.)
fix: Either remove the orphan swatch (the same hex is already shown inside the first step row) or give it explicit meaning: enlarge it to ~48px, set it as a header swatch with a label ('Primary colour: #0E4A8A · Custom mix'), or move it inline next to the recipe name. If kept, add aria-label="Primary colour swatch: #0E4A8A".

principle: WCAG 2.2 §4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
location: /wishlist quick-add '+' submit button (no aria-label, visible glyph only); /library detail-panel 'copy' hex button (no aria-label, ambiguous verb); /recipes/[id] paint-slot picker button ('Custom · #0e4a8a ▾', no aria-label); /tools/gradient hex inputs (no aria-label, already in UX-019); various icon-only chip buttons
problem: Multiple interactive controls have either no accessible name or a name that lacks target context. The /wishlist '+' submit button announces as 'plus, button' (same pattern as UX-008 from the first audit, different surface). The /library detail-panel 'copy' button announces as 'copy, button' — copy what? The paint-slot picker on /recipes/[id] is announced only as the visible label which includes the hex but not the role ('change paint' is the action).
fix: Add aria-label on each: wishlist '+' → aria-label="Add wishlist item"; library 'copy' → aria-label="Copy hex code <hex>" (dynamic), or keep visible 'copy' and add aria-label="Copy hex"; paint-slot picker → aria-label="Change paint for step". Trivial attribute additions, no layout impact.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.4.1 Use of Color; Refactoring UI — Color is not the only channel
location: /tools/match — per-row ΔE indicator (small coloured dot before the ΔE number: green = <2 perceptually identical, amber = <5 acceptable, grey = ≥5 distant)
problem: Match quality is communicated solely by dot colour. The legend ('Green dot = ΔE < 2, amber < 5, grey ≥ 5') is in the page subtitle, which scrolls out of view. A user with red-green deficiency cannot distinguish a 'perceptually identical' match from an 'acceptable' one at a glance. The ΔE number is present (1.8, 4.5, etc.) but its interpretation requires remembering the thresholds.
fix: Layer a second visual channel on top of colour: a check ✓ glyph for ΔE<2, a tilde ~ for <5, a × or dash for ≥5; or pair the dot with a short text tag ('CLOSE', 'OK', 'FAR'). Add a permanent compact legend chip beside the Results header so the meaning is recoverable without scrolling. Single-component change in MatchResultRow.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of System Status; Material 3 — disabled-state semantics
location: /library — FilterRail INVENTORY 'Owned only' checkbox (disabled until P2.3 ships, opacity:0.5, cursor:not-allowed, title="Enables with P2.3")
problem: The 'Owned only' inventory filter is a permanently-disabled checkbox carrying a tooltip 'Enables with P2.3'. The tooltip is invisible until hover, and the visible state is just opacity:0.5 — indistinguishable from a future-active filter at a quick glance. Painters who own a lot of inventory will keep trying to use this filter and silently failing. Same pattern as UX-005 from the first audit (the [ edit ] disabled control on the project page).
fix: Either (a) hide the 'Owned only' control entirely until P2.3 ships (recommended — premature affordance is worse than missing affordance), or (b) add a visible 'soon' badge inline ('Owned only ⌛ soon') and make the disabled state unambiguous (opacity:0.4 + strikethrough or italic). Either way, the title-tooltip alone is insufficient.

principle: Refactoring UI — design for real content; Apple HIG Clarity (no truncation when space exists)
location: /tools/gradient — ramp swatch labels truncate paint names ('Prussian Blue Lig…', 'British Royal Blu…', 'Cygnar Blue Highl…') even though there is significant horizontal whitespace below each swatch
problem: Each ramp step shows a 200px-wide swatch with the paint name beneath in a single truncated line. Long paint names like 'Prussian Blue Light' or 'Cygnar Blue Highlight' cut off mid-word as 'Prussian Blue Lig…'. The cards have plenty of vertical room and the paint name is the actual deliverable of the tool — the user wants to know what to buy.
fix: Allow the paint name to wrap to two lines (remove single-line truncation, set line-clamp-2 if a cap is needed). Show the brand name on a second muted line so 'Citadel · Caledor Sky' / 'P3 Formula · Cygnar Blue Highlight' both fit. Failing that, widen each swatch column or reduce the default step count from 5 to 4 to leave more room.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency & Standards; Refactoring UI — one semantic = one visual
location: /recipes empty state — '[ + ] Create your first recipe' CTA button text appears clipped at the right edge of the bordered card (last character of 'recipe' clips through the border)
problem: The CTA button inside the recipes empty state has insufficient horizontal padding — the visible '[ + ] Create your first recipe' text touches/clips the right border of the button frame. Small polish issue but stands out because it is the focal action of the empty state and the only interactive control in view.
fix: Increase horizontal padding on the empty-state CTA button by 1-2 spacing steps (e.g. px-3 → px-4 or px-5). The empty state is a known-narrow viewport for this content; the CTA should never feel cramped.
